maria: Heads-up: saw repeated ~200-400ms p99 latency pulses on a long-context streambench run ( > 1M tokens / host ). Feels like KV reuse TTL skew + eviction waterfall.

aj: ugh. repro script or logs?

maria: quick sample from the shard where it happened:
```
[2026-11-03T03:12:19Z] inference: req_id=abcd kv_insert=512KB ttl=300s reuse_hit=0
[2026-11-03T03:12:21Z] inference: req_id=abce kv_insert=1.1MB ttl=300s reuse_hit=0
[2026-11-03T03:12:22Z] pager: evicted=128 entries -> spike latency +240ms
[2026-11-03T03:12:22Z] perf: kv_lock waitns=2350
```

maria: pattern: long traces where sequence length drifts upward, then a cluster of large KV inserts happens, pager kicks in and we get a ~200-400ms tail pulse every ~30-90s.

liam: can you share vmstat/meminfo around the pulse? sounds like fragmentation or bump-alloc causing slowdown.

maria: attaching trimmed metrics: free_pages drops from 4300 -> 1200 then pager rate ~800 evictions/s for 200ms window. heap fragmentation metric (slab_free_ratio) drops 0.67 -> 0.22.

nina: interesting — did we recently change kernel selection or attention kernel for long contexts? that could change per-call KV size.

maria: yes, around the same deploy we switched to fused-attn kernel for medium sequences which ups the per-step KV writes because we now materialize denser key tensors prefetching. Not huge in steady state but under bursty long-context workloads it amplifies paging.

aj: hypothesis: per-request KV write size distribution now has a heavier tail -> LRU policy reorders evict victims such that we do many small reinserts causing pager churn. FIFO might behave better under that write-skew.

liam: did you try forcing FIFO for a quick A/B?

maria: flipped to FIFO on a canary for one shard for 2 hours: p95 unchanged, p99 pulse amplitude fell ~35% and frequency reduced by ~2x. downside: average reuse_rate down 8%.

dave: tradeoff makes sense. FIFO avoids frequent reinsert churn when large writes create many new slabs that immediately become hot again. LRU keeps bringing them to front and pushes out smaller long-lived entries.

nina: what about correctness concerns? any observed misrouting or stale KV reads after FIFO?

maria: none seen. we have unit tests for access-order invariants and checksums passed. the only odd was momentary growth in resident set due to FIFO delaying reclaim on some shards, but within budget.

aj: profiled the kernel: perf reported heavy time in kv_reclaim_scan and spin on kv_bucket_mutex during the pulse. batching heuristics also matter — when batching groups grew (we raised batch window slightly), we generated denser KV writes and exacerbated the churn.

liam: so two knobs: eviction policy + batching window. maybe add adaptive batch window that constrains per-request kv_bytes when resident > watermark? keeps write fanout down.

maria: implemented a quick limiter: if kv_bytes_to_write > 512KB && resident > 70% -> cap to 512KB and fall back to partial streaming write. Canary looked good, p99 pulses reduced and throughput unchanged.

dave: long-term we should add a reuse-aware eviction policy: track reuse_score by entry size and recency, prefer evicting large cold slabs. avoids evicting lots of small hot entries.

nina: agree. also add a TTL skew monitor in Console: alert if reuse_hit drops >30% concurrently with pager evict spikes.

maria: action items:
- aj: roll FIFO canary to second region and collect 48h metrics (A/B).
- liam: prototype reuse-aware eviction heuristic (size-weighted) + eval sim.
- nina: Console alert for reuse/pager correlation.
- dave: PR for adaptive batch cap (already WIP).

aj: I'll also run a kernel-level microbenchmark to see how fused-attn changes kv_write_size distribution and push results here.

evict-bot: pager_alert: shard=shard-17 severity=warn evict_rate=750/s window=180ms resident_pct=73 reuse_rate_drop=38%

maria: thanks all — keeping an eye on canary metrics. will post follow-up with traces and flamegraphs. :thumbsup:
